scenes.text: Mary is eighty-one and lives alone. Her daughter Anna has explained the morning a hundred times. Alongside is for the hundred and first.
Anna's side is a website. Mary's routines, what she has reported, and anything asking for attention.
Anna describes breakfast the way she would say it to a neighbour, and attaches the photo that makes it obvious which container she means.
It does not invent the steps. It asks for them.
She gives them, including what to say if the container is not there. That becomes an approved alternative: the only answer the assistant is allowed to offer.
She changes the time by saying so. Then she reviews exactly what the assistant will say and what the television will show, and publishes. Nothing runs until she does.
Next morning, on the television. Breakfast, the photo Anna attached, and one instruction at a time.
Mary asks what she is having. The voice client and the television show the same approved answer, because they read the same backend.
She asks for fifteen minutes. This morning moves. The recurring routine does not.
She comes back, and Alongside picks up at the step she actually confirmed. Showing a step was never the same as finishing it.
The container is not there. That is Anna's own sentence, approved in advance. When Alongside does not know, it says so rather than guessing.
It is on Anna's dashboard immediately, with the activity and the step attached. It does not claim to have sent a message it never sent.
Later she says she has eaten. Every screen agrees on the same final state.

scenes.source: card:Tell it once. Review it.|Help my family member through their day.
scenes.text: One backend. Three surfaces that cannot disagree. Alongside.
